Title: Diagnosis of test `testOverrideGeoMeanWithMathClass`

Details:
The test `testOverrideGeoMeanWithMathClass` creates a `SummaryStatistics` instance and overrides its geometric mean implementation with a new `GeometricMean` object using `setGeoMeanImpl(new GeometricMean())`. It then adds several values and expects the geometric mean calculated by `SummaryStatistics` to match the result of a standalone `GeometricMean` evaluation on the same values.

From the code, the `SummaryStatistics.setGeoMeanImpl` method sets the internal `geoMeanImpl` to the new implementation and calls `checkEmpty()` which verifies the internal state is empty before replacing. Thus, the override is allowed only when the statistics are empty.

The `addValue` method in `SummaryStatistics` calls `geoMeanImpl.increment(value)` to feed each new value to the geometric mean calculation, but only if `geoMeanImpl` is not the default `GeometricMean` implementation (i.e., if it was overridden, it is incremented).

The `GeometricMean.increment(double)` method delegates the update to an internal `sumOfLogs` statistic, while `GeometricMean.getResult()` calculates the geometric mean using the exponent of the average of the logged values.

The failing test suggests that when the override is applied by the test, the `geoMeanImpl` implementation inside `SummaryStatistics` is updated but the values added are not properly reflected in the overridden `GeometricMean`, or the expected result does not match due to synchronization or state update issues.

In the context of `SynchronizedSummaryStatistics`, the `setGeoMeanImpl` is overridden as a synchronized method that calls the superclass. Hence, synchronization should not be the issue unless state consistency between `SynchronizedSummaryStatistics` and its contained implementations is compromised.

The root cause is likely that after overriding the `geoMeanImpl` with a fresh `GeometricMean`, the values added subsequently do not correctly update internal states, or the state is not properly cleared or reset when the implementation is changed, causing discrepancies between the expected and actual geometric mean result.

The test failure might be due to the `checkEmpty()` method preventing override if not empty, or the internal states of the new `GeometricMean` not being reset properly on override.

Methods to investigate or fix would involve the `SummaryStatistics.setGeoMeanImpl`, `SummaryStatistics.addValue`, and possibly `SynchronizedSummaryStatistics.setGeoMeanImpl` to ensure correct state management and updates post override.

Suggested methods to fix:
org.apache.commons.math.stat.descriptive.SummaryStatistics.setGeoMeanImpl(org.apache.commons.math.stat.descriptive.StorelessUnivariateStatistic)
org.apache.commons.math.stat.descriptive.SummaryStatistics.addValue(double)
org.apache.commons.math.stat.descriptive.SynchronizedSummaryStatistics.setGeoMeanImpl(org.apache.commons.math.stat.descriptive.StorelessUnivariateStatistic)
